newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO firms amid tight supplies.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO firms amid tight supplies.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Wednesday were firmer as a buyer emerged in a tight market, traders said.

A Singapore trader bid for 20,000 tonnes of 180-cst fuel oil at $124 per tonne for January 8-12 lifting but only faced a seller, a major, for a later lifting for January 13-17 at $124.50, who eventually sold to the trader at $124.00.
Indications were higher than $119-$121 per tonne on Tuesday.
Swaps were unchanged from Tuesday's levels with Janaury talked at $120.50/$121.50 a tonne.
Traders said they expected cargo levels to be supported until the end of December as Chinese buyers have held off buying supplies prior to the Chinese New Year in February.
Chinese buyers were quiet as offers have been too high with rising freight costs.
A cargo was sold into southern China late last week at $131 per tonne cost-and-freight South China for January delivery, traders said.
But one South Korean refiner said there were at least two to four cargoes available from South Korea in January but could not sell into China with freight as high as $8 per tonne.
A Kuwaiti 380-cst cargo was also heard offered for Janaury arrival at $2.25 per barrel over Singapore spot quotes, c-and-f Singapore but bids were at $1.75.
But some traders were skeptical, citing the softening of crude prices after the rally.
In the swaps market, the prompt December paper was supported at $122.50/$123.50, up from Monday's $122.25 bid. But January swaps were quoted at $120/$121, slightly lower from $120.50/$122 on Monday.
One Singapore trader told Reuters he was keen to sell his Janaury lifting barrels but could not find any buyers.
But other traders agreed that Chinese oil demand continued healthy for January. They expected enquiries to slow at the end of the week.
Most South Korean barrels for January loading were heard to have been sold out.
